Ruins
rōō´ĭnz
n. pl. (fallen remains; rendering Hebrew harisuth)
From Latin ruere, to fall. Ruins are what a building becomes; Scripture's interest is chiefly in who rebuilds them.

Biblical Definition

Ruins are fallen remains. Amos prophesies restoration in exactly these terms: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old” (Amo 9:11) — a text James quotes at the Jerusalem council to justify receiving Gentiles (Act 15:16). Isaiah promises that they shall “build the old wastes… and they shall repair the waste cities” (Isa 61:4).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines ruin as destruction; fall; overthrow; defeat; and the remains of a decayed or demolished city, house, fortress, or any work of men.

expand to see more

RUIN, n. Destruction; fall; overthrow; defeat; that change of any thing which destroys it, or entirely defeats its object.

2. The remains of a decayed or demolished city, house, fortress, or any work of men or of nature.

3. The state of being destroyed; the state of being decayed or having lost its former excellence.

Key Scripture

Amo 9:11 — "In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old:"

Act 15:16 — "After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down; and I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up:"

Isa 61:4 — "And they shall build the old wastes, they shall raise up the former desolations, and they shall repair the waste cities, the desolations of many generations."

Luk 6:49 — "But he that heareth, and doeth not, is like a man that without a foundation built an house upon the earth; against which the stream did beat vehemently, and immediately it fell; and the ruin of that house was great."

Modern Corruption

Restoration is imagined as replacement, and both Amos and Isaiah promise something stranger — the old ruins themselves raised and repaired.

expand to see more

Amos 9:11 is precise about the material: I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old. Not a new tabernacle on a clear site — the fallen thing raised. James used this at the Jerusalem council to explain why Gentiles were streaming in without becoming Jews: the rebuilding of David's fallen tent was always meant to include the residue of men, and the nations, upon whom my name is called.

Isaiah 61:4 assigns the work to the very people who had been comforted: they shall build the old wastes, they shall raise up the former desolations, and they shall repair the waste cities, the desolations of many generations. The mourners of Zion, given beauty for ashes, become the builders. That is the pattern — those who have been restored are the ones handed the trowel.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew harisuth (H2034), ruins; haras (H2040), to tear down; Greek kataskapto (G2679), to dig down, in Acts 15:16.

expand to see more

Hebrew harisuth (H2034) — ruins; only Amos 9:11.

Hebrew chorbah (H2723) — waste, desolation; Isaiah 61:4, the old wastes.

Greek kataskapto (G2679) — ruined, dug down; Acts 15:16.

Usage

"“I will raise up his ruins” — the fallen thing rebuilt, not replaced."

"“They shall repair the waste cities” — the comforted handed the trowel."

"“The ruin of that house was great” — the house built without a foundation."
